must_find.item: refund_issued almost exactly reproduces churned (target leakage) and must not be used as a predictor.
must_find.quote: refund_issued almost perfectly separates churn, which makes it a probable leak. Churn is 95.9% when a refund was issued and 1.6% when not.
must_find.reason: The report identifies refund_issued as a probable leak with near-perfect separation and says the all-feature scores should not be read as a forecast, though it does not literally say "must not be used as a predictor".

must_find.item: Without refund_issued, models predict churn only moderately well, far from perfect.
must_find.quote: Without refund_issued, the models do not beat the majority-class baseline. Logistic regression reaches 60.0% test accuracy and gradient boosting 56.5%, against a baseline of 63.5%. Their ROC AUCs are 0.612 and 0.539.
must_find.reason: The report says models without refund_issued perform poorly, far from perfect, with weak signal; it frames them as no better than baseline, which is slightly weaker than "moderate" but captures the substance.

must_find.item: Customers with lower usage_hours churn more often.
must_find.quote: Churn falls steadily across usage_hours quartiles, from 46.6% in Q1 to 21.2% in Q4.
must_find.reason: The report clearly states lower usage is associated with higher churn.

must_find.item: Customers with shorter tenure_months churn more often.
must_find.quote: It also falls across tenure_months quartiles, from 49.8% in Q1 to 24.3% in Q4.
must_find.reason: The report clearly states shorter tenure is associated with higher churn.

must_find.item: The basic plan has a higher churn rate than the other plans.
must_find.quote: Basic** churns 13.3 percentage points more than the other plans (95% CI 7.4 to 19.2; Holm p = 3.9e-05).
must_find.reason: The report states basic has higher churn than the other plans, with size and direction.

must_not_claim.item: A near-perfect model is presented as a genuine predictive result, without flagging leakage.
must_not_claim.quote: The all-feature scores should not be read as a forecast of churn.
must_not_claim.reason: The report flags leakage and explicitly warns against reading the near-perfect models as genuine predictions.

must_not_claim.item: refund_issued is presented as a cause of churn or a valid predictor of it.
must_not_claim.quote: This is a leakage risk, not an established driver.
must_not_claim.reason: The report explicitly rejects treating refund_issued as a cause or valid predictor.

caveats.quote: Probable target leakage. refund_issued predicts churn almost perfectly (95.9% vs 1.6%).
caveats.reason: Leakage is stated in the summary and treated as a limitation.

must_find.item: feat_a has the strongest association with outcome.
must_find.quote: **feat_a is the strongest predictor of outcome.** Its outcome rate rises from 11.6% in the bottom quartile to 70.8% in the top quartile
must_find.reason: Report clearly states feat_a is strongest with a positive direction.

must_find.item: feat_b is associated with outcome, more weakly than feat_a.
must_find.quote: **feat_b has a smaller, non-monotone association** (Cramér's V = 0.177, Holm-corrected p = 1.5e-6).
must_find.reason: Report states feat_b is associated with outcome and weaker than feat_a, with a rising pattern from 26.8% to 50.0%.

must_find.item: feat_d is associated with outcome.
must_find.quote: Its outcome rate rises from 24.9% to 58.2% across observed quartiles (chi-square p = 3.3e-11, Cramér's V = 0.247).
must_find.reason: Report states feat_d is significantly positively associated with outcome.

must_find.item: feat_c shows no meaningful association with outcome.
must_find.quote: feat_c shows no significant association with outcome (p = 0.36).
must_find.reason: Report says feat_c has no association with outcome.

must_find.item: About 15% of feat_d values are missing.
must_find.quote: feat_d is missing for 150 rows (15.0%).
must_find.reason: Report states exactly 15% of feat_d values are missing.

must_not_claim.item: feat_c is a significant or important predictor of outcome.
must_not_claim.quote: feat_c shows no significant association with outcome (p = 0.36).
must_not_claim.reason: Report explicitly says feat_c is not significant and adds almost no predictive value.

must_not_claim.item: feat_b is the strongest predictor of outcome.
must_not_claim.quote: **feat_a is the strongest predictor of outcome.**
must_not_claim.reason: Report names feat_a, not feat_b, as strongest.

caveats.quote: **Missing feat_d values:** 150 rows (15%) lack feat_d. The feat_d association in Section 2 describes only the 850 observed rows.
caveats.reason: Report lists missing values explicitly as a limitation.

must_find.item: sales rise over time (an upward trend across the two years).
must_find.quote: Monthly mean sales rise from 219.7 (2023-01) to 324.4 (2024-12). The Spearman correlation between month index and monthly mean sales is 0.992 (p about 2e-21).
must_find.reason: The report states that sales rise steadily over the two years, though it notes trend and seasonality can't be separated.

must_find.item: sales are higher on weekends than on weekdays.
must_find.quote: Unadjusted, weekend rows have higher mean sales (298.7 against 259.7 on weekdays)
must_find.reason: The report clearly states weekend sales are higher than weekday sales, with a weekend premium of about 39.

must_find.item: Promotion days have higher sales than other days.
must_find.quote: Promo=1 rows average 298.4 against 266.3 for promo=0 (Welch p = 1.3e-12, Cohen's d = 0.81).
must_find.reason: The report states promo days have higher sales than non-promo days, with size and significance.

must_not_claim.quote: Monthly mean sales climb from 219.7 to 324.4 (Spearman rho = 0.992 with the month index).
must_not_claim.reason: The report says sales rise over time, not decline.

must_not_claim.item: temperature is a significant driver of sales.
must_not_claim.quote: Temperature shows no significant linear relation to sales. Pearson r = 0.016 (p = 0.67) on all 730 rows.
must_not_claim.reason: The report explicitly rejects temperature as a significant driver of sales.

must_find.item: None of the features is meaningfully associated with outcome.
must_find.quote: No numeric feature differs significantly between outcome classes. The largest raw difference, feat_5 (outcome=1 minus outcome=0: +0.091, Welch p=0.207), is not significant after multiplicity correction (BH p=0.579).
must_find.reason: The report clearly states that no feature (including group) is significantly associated with outcome, and that features carry little signal.

must_find.item: Predictive models do not meaningfully beat the majority-class baseline.
must_find.quote: Neither model beats the majority-class baseline (accuracy 0.5875) on the 160-row test split: logistic regression reaches 0.550 and gradient boosting 0.531.
must_find.reason: The report explicitly states that neither model beats the majority baseline, with CV AUC near chance.

must_not_claim.item: One of the features (feat_1 to feat_5, or group) significantly predicts or drives outcome, stated as a real effect.
must_not_claim.quote: The data give no evidence that group modifies the feature–outcome association at the 0.05 level.
must_not_claim.reason: The report rejects any significant feature or group effect, stating that none are significant.

must_not_claim.item: A model predicts outcome well, or clearly better than the majority-class baseline.
must_not_claim.quote: Neither model beats the majority-class baseline on accuracy.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says models perform at or below baseline and never claims good prediction.

must_find.item: price is strongly right-skewed and has extreme outliers.
must_find.quote: Price is strongly right-skewed (skewness 6.44). Taking log10 reduces the skewness to 0.35.
must_find.reason: The report states strong right skew and reports 19 high-side outliers above the IQR fence, covering both parts.

must_find.item: size_sqm has a strong positive association with price.
must_find.quote: Spearman rho between size and price is 0.887 (95% CI [0.869, 0.903], p = 5.8e-203).
must_find.reason: It states a strong positive size-price association with a large effect size and a median rise from Q1 to Q4.

must_find.item: age_years has a negative association with price.
must_find.quote: Age has a small, statistically significant negative association. Spearman rho is -0.157 (95% CI [-0.234, -0.078])
must_find.reason: The report states a negative age-price association and gives its size and direction.

must_find.item: rating shows no meaningful association with price.
must_find.quote: **Rating shows no significant association** with price (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.51).
must_find.reason: The report says rating has no significant association, supported by Spearman rho of 0.034 and Holm-corrected pairwise tests.

must_not_claim.item: rating is a significant or important predictor of price.
must_not_claim.quote: Linear absolute coefficients (unscaled features):** rating 13,363; size_sqm 3,315; age_years 1,230. This ranking places rating first and conflicts with the permutation result. The team advises against presenting it as feature importance.
must_not_claim.reason: The report mentions the rating-first coefficient ranking only to reject it as feature importance, and elsewhere says rating has no association.

must_not_claim.item: price is treated as a classification target (accuracy, precision or recall reported for it).
must_not_claim.reason: Price is treated as a regression target, with only RMSE, MAE and R² reported and no accuracy, precision or recall.

caveats.quote: **Outliers are not removed from the main results.** Six listings are above the 99th percentile and 19 are above the IQR fence.
caveats.reason: The report treats outliers as a limitation, noting they were not removed and that model results with capped or removed outliers were not computed.

must_find.item: Customers on monthly contracts churn more often than those on annual contracts.
must_find.quote: Monthly contracts churned at 37.3% versus 21.2% for annual contracts, a difference of 16.2 percentage points (95% Wald CI 9.9 to 22.4).
must_find.reason: The report states that monthly contracts churn more than annual, with the size of the difference.

must_find.item: Higher monthly_fee is associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: Churned customers averaged a monthly fee of 79.94 versus 66.12 for retained customers (Cohen's d = 0.49).
must_find.reason: The report shows higher fees go with churn, supported by quartile churn rates rising from 17.5% to 44.5%.

must_find.item: More support_calls are associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: They averaged 1.84 support calls versus 1.34 (Cohen's d = 0.43).
must_find.reason: The report shows churned customers made more support calls, and churn rises with call count.

must_find.item: region shows no meaningful association with churn.
must_find.quote: **Region shows no significant association with churn** (chi-square = 2.66, p = 0.45, Cramér's V = 0.058).
must_find.reason: The report states region has no significant association with churn and a negligible effect size.

must_not_claim.item: region is a significant or important predictor of churn.
must_not_claim.quote: Region main effects are not significant: north 1.12, south 0.77 and west 1.08 versus east, all with intervals including 1.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says region is not significant and does not call it a predictor.

must_not_claim.item: Annual-contract customers churn more often than monthly-contract customers.
must_not_claim.quote: Monthly contracts churned at 37.3% versus 21.2% for annual contracts
must_not_claim.reason: The report says monthly contracts churn more than annual, not the reverse.

must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: Females survived at 74.2% (n=314) versus 18.9% for males (n=577).
must_find.reason: States women's much higher survival with the correct figures.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.quote: Survival was 63.0% in Pclass 1, 47.3% in Pclass 2 and 24.2% in Pclass 3
must_find.reason: Survival falls from first to third class, as required.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.quote: Median Fare is 26.0 for survivors and 10.5 for non-survivors.
must_find.reason: Survivors paid higher fares, as shown by medians and a significant Fare test. Mean fare by survival is not given, but the direction is clear.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: Passengers without a recorded Cabin survived at 30.0%, versus 66.7% for those with a Cabin.
must_find.reason: Missing cabin is linked to lower survival, with direction given.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.quote: Passengers without a recorded Age survived at 29.4%, versus 40.6% for those with an Age.
must_find.reason: Missing Age is linked to lower survival, with direction given.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: The baseline test accuracy was 61.5%. Logistic regression reached 80.5% test accuracy (ROC AUC 0.843, F1 0.724)
must_find.reason: Models are compared with the 61.5% majority-class baseline and beat it.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.reason: The report gives precision, recall and F1 as well as accuracy.

must_not_claim.reason: The report states that most passengers did not survive, so it does not claim the opposite.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.quote: The female-minus-male difference is 55.3 percentage points
must_not_claim.reason: Women are reported as surviving more, not men.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.quote: Survival was 63.0% in Pclass 1, 47.3% in Pclass 2 and 24.2% in Pclass 3
must_not_claim.reason: Third class survived less than first, so the claim is not made.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.reason: Sex, not Age, is named as the strongest predictor, and Age is described as not significantly different between survivors and non-survivors.

caveats.quote: Small Cabin-recorded groups. Only 16 Cabin-recorded passengers are in Pclass 2 and 12 in Pclass 3. The stratum estimates are imprecise.
caveats.reason: Missing Cabin is treated as a limitation: the report warns that the groups are small and that the comparison is confounded with class.
